# Sandbox environments

Crush derives repository layout from the working directory and uses it for the data directory and for bash sandbox writable paths. This document shows those values for a plain directory, a main checkout, and a linked worktree. Paths under the temporary test root appear as <tmp>.

## Global config

Every environment below loads this global crush.json, which lives in the test's global config directory. Its sandbox settings apply to all three working directories.

```json
{
  "options": {
    "sandbox": {
      "mode": "auto",
      "writable_paths": ["/srv/shared-cache"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Config and bash options

Each row is one working directory. The git columns come from the loaded config, the data directory is where session state lives, and the writable paths are what sandboxed bash commands may write to. In the linked worktree, the main checkout's git directory is added so git commands can update refs and worktree metadata.

| Environment | Worktree root | Main checkout | Linked common dir | Data directory | Sandbox mode | Writable paths |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plain directory | - | - | - | <tmp>/plain/.crush | auto | /srv/shared-cache |
| Main checkout | <tmp>/main | <tmp>/main | - | <tmp>/main/.crush | auto | /srv/shared-cache |
| Linked worktree | <tmp>/linked | <tmp>/main | <tmp>/main/.git | <tmp>/main/.crush | auto | /srv/shared-cache, <tmp>/main/.git |
